name: Chien Chung-Wei (簡忠威)
fit_reason: atmospheric urban and interior watercolor, quiet scenes, strong tonal control. Built international credibility from a Taiwan base through IWS competitions.
use_as: Primary career-path reference for building international watercolor credibility from an Asian base.

name: Keiko Tanabe
fit_reason: Japanese watercolor painter, urban and travel subjects, light and understated atmosphere. Has exhibited with AWS and NWS — Japan-rooted identity with international visibility.
use_as: Reference for Japan-origin watercolor career with international reach.

name: Thomas W. Schaller
fit_reason: Architectural watercolor — buildings, urban light, atmosphere, quiet structural observation. Large-format architectural studies with dramatic mood.
use_as: Primary reference for architectural watercolor practice and aesthetic.

name: Cathy Read
fit_reason: British architectural watercolorist known for Edinburgh and UK urban scenes. Has exhibited in London and internationally.
use_as: Reference for building an architectural watercolor career with direct-to-collector sales.

name: Lian Quan Zhen
fit_reason: Chinese-born watercolorist integrating Chinese ink painting sensibility with Western watercolor technique. AWS member.
use_as: Reference for cross-cultural watercolor identity — Chinese training meeting international exhibition contexts.

name: Japan Watercolor Society (日本水彩画会) exhibitors
fit_reason: Annual national exhibition — Tier 3 credibility target. Contemporary Japanese watercolor practitioners working at the level she is building toward.
use_as: Reference ecosystem for Japan active watercolor exhibition community.

name: Alvaro Castagnet
fit_reason: Urban watercolor with loose, atmospheric style; strong international exhibition record built from a non-Western base. AWS signature member.
use_as: Reference for building international watercolor exhibition record through society competitions.

name: Jean Haines
fit_reason: Prominent UK watercolor practitioner and author. Style is loose and expressive — very different from your quiet urban register. Community reference only.
use_as: Community reference only. Do NOT use as stylistic reference or aesthetic comparison.

name: Samantha Dion Baker
fit_reason: Keeps a daily illustrated sketch journal of ordinary life — her home, her neighborhood, meals, small domestic moments — painted in watercolor and pen, the same daily-diary practice you has kept since 2020. Her journal grew directly into a series of published books (Draw Your Day), the publication path you is building toward.
shared_traits: diary that grew into published books
use_as: Closest model for turning a daily watercolor diary into published books and a sustaining illustration career.

name: Liz Steel
fit_reason: A daily watercolor sketchbook artist from Sydney who paints her own life — her cat, teacups, the rooms she sits in, the buildings she passes — and has built a large following and a teaching practice around that habit. The everyday-domestic register and the cat as a recurring anchor closely echo your diary.
shared_traits: cats and domestic life as subjects
use_as: Reference for sustaining a daily watercolor practice and turning the habit itself into a community and income.

name: Ohn Mar Win
fit_reason: A Burmese-British watercolorist who fills sketchbooks with domestic still life — coffee, food, the quiet objects of home — and shares them daily on Instagram, where she has built a large following and a self-published book. An Asian-heritage artist whose career rests on watercolor sketchbooks and an online audience, much like your.
shared_traits: domestic still life and home objects
use_as: Reference for building an illustration career on watercolor sketchbooks, an online following, and self-published books.

name: Tatsuro Kiuchi (木内達朗)
fit_reason: A Tokyo illustrator whose quiet scenes — cafes, apartments, interior light, figures alone in domestic space — share your stillness and attention to ordinary moments. He works digitally rather than in watercolor, so this is a thematic and tonal kinship more than a material one, but few artists match her register of calm domestic observation so closely.
use_as: Stylistic and tonal reference for quiet, domestic, interior-light storytelling; note the medium is digital, not watercolor.

name: Felicia Chiao
fit_reason: A Taiwanese-American illustrator who keeps a deeply personal sketchbook diary of interior, introspective domestic scenes and built an audience of hundreds of thousands from that practice alone — moving from a day job into a full illustration and gallery career. Her medium is marker rather than watercolor, so the kinship is the diary practice, the domestic-interior subject, and the online-built path, not the surface look.
shared_traits: career built from an online audience
use_as: Reference for how a private daily sketchbook diary can grow into a full illustration and exhibition career; note medium is marker, not watercolor.

name: Mateusz Urbanowicz
fit_reason: A Tokyo-based painter whose watercolor series of ordinary Tokyo storefronts and streets grew from Instagram into published art books and a sustaining independent career — almost exactly the trajectory you is on. He is Polish rather than Asian, so the overlap is the practice and path: watercolor, quiet Tokyo, online audience to art books.
shared_traits: online audience grown into art books
use_as: Direct career-path model: watercolor of everyday Tokyo, built from Instagram into published art books and self-sustaining practice.

name: Aeppol (애뽈)
fit_reason: A Korean illustrator who built the long-running 'Forest Girl's Diary' from a personal blog — a soft, watercolor-style daily diary of a girl's quiet life, updated several times a week — and turned it into bestselling published books. The subject is a fairy-tale forest rather than a Tokyo apartment, so the kinship is the daily-diary engine and the online-to-books path, not the setting.
shared_traits: Asian illustrator built from online audience
use_as: Reference for sustaining a named daily-diary project over years and turning it into a publishing career; the diary format, not the fairy-tale content, is the parallel.

name: Yuko Higuchi (ヒグチユウコ)
fit_reason: A Tokyo painter whose work centers on cats, rendered in watercolor and ink, and who has built a prolific publishing practice — art books, picture books, a gallery-shop of her own — alongside a large following. Her world is surreal and fantastical rather than quiet-domestic, so the kinship is the cat-centered subject and the art-book/publishing career, not the realist register.
use_as: Reference for a cats-centered Tokyo painter building a deep art-book and publishing career; note the style is surreal/fantasy, not realist domestic.

name: Zao Dao (早稻)
fit_reason: A self-taught Chinese illustrator from Guangdong who built her audience on a Weibo blog from 2010 and turned it into internationally published art books (Song of Sylvan, Ink of Wild) and gallery shows abroad — a Chinese artist who reached an international career through ink-and-watercolor work and an online following. Her imagery is folkloric and fantastical, so the kinship is the Chinese-artist-online-to-art-books path, not the subject.
use_as: Reference for a Chinese illustrator building from an online following to internationally published art books and overseas exhibitions; the path, not the fantasy subject, is the parallel.
